preregistration.note: This file holds INPUTS only: literature reference values, tolerances and the declared model. It contains no value computed by this application, and tests refuse a key that could carry one. The measured artifact and the gate outcome are a separate, later commit. Changing any value below changes criteria_hash or reference_bundle_hash, so an old validation record can never authorize a result computed under different criteria.

model_under_test.dispersion: none (no preset offers it; provenance only)
model_under_test.convergence: as built by OrcaQuantumEngineProvider.build_input for calc_type 'opt' (no tightened settings); the exact input text of every job is hashed into the artifact
model_under_test.rationale: PBE0 def2-TZVP is the higher-quality of the offered presets. It is a proposal, not a claim that the default B3LYP def2-SVP is inadequate; this benchmark is what establishes that. Validation authorizes percentages ONLY for this method/basis, because method_basis is part of model_version.

gates.ranking_rule: pairwise_tie_aware: for a pair whose reference values differ by at least reference_tie_kcal the computed energies must order the same way; a closer pair is unordered
gates.quantitative_rule: one absolute error per reference-listed tautomer after rebaselining each vector to its own lowest reference-listed tautomer; a system passes only if its MAE <= mae_tolerance_kcal AND its max error <= max_error_tolerance_kcal

tolerance_evidence: Tolerances (tie 1.0, MAE 1.0, max 2.0 kcal/mol) were proposed in the approved plan of 2026-10-02, BEFORE the supplied papers were read, and are not changed here. The evidence below is context for plausibility, not a derivation.

Method spread inside one source: Belova 2014 SI gives the acetylacetone diketo-enol electronic energy as 4.849 (MP2/cc-pVTZ) and 6.481 (B3LYP/aug-cc-pVTZ) kcal/mol, a spread of 1.63 between two large-basis levels.

Cytosine 3a is not settled between sources: Trygubenko 2002 puts it 3.68 above 2a; Fogarasi 2008 (a citation of CCSD(T) ranges, read for this purpose) places it near 1.5-2.1 above 2b, about 1 kcal/mol closer.

Rotamer and isomer limits of a single start geometry: cytosine 2a/2b differ by 0.69 and 3a/3b by 1.57 kcal/mol, and RDKit does not enumerate hydroxyl rotamers or C=N-H E/Z, so the application may land on the higher variant. The reference value of a tautomer is its LOWEST variant (see representative_rule), so this limitation can only raise an error.

2-pyridone/2-hydroxypyridine: Goller 2022 Table 4 gives 2.07 (cc-pVQZ), 1.96 (CBS 3/4) and 2.48 (CBS 2/3) kcal/mol for the same pair, so the reference itself moves by about 0.5; Rendell 1993's 1.4/0.76 kcal/mol (two small bases, SCF geometries) lie further away.

DISCLOSED BEFORE THE RUN: the same Goller 2022 paper (Table 6) lists PBE0-D3(BJ)/def2-TZVP electronic energies for this pair that put 2-pyridone 0.32 kcal/mol BELOW 2-hydroxypyridine, against a reference that puts it 2.07 above. If the application reproduces that, the 2-pyridone system misses both the ranking gate and the maximum-error tolerance. The tolerances were not loosened and the system was not demoted to optional because of it; a gate that fails here is the intended, recorded outcome.

Fogarasi 2010 sets a 0.5 kcal/mol benchmark-accuracy goal for converged reference values; that is a methodology target for the REFERENCE, not a threshold for two independent DFT energies being the same.

systems.name: Cytosine, gas phase (three application-level tautomers)

source.locator: Table 2, last line, Etot(CCSD(T)/inf); structures from Fig. 1

reference.method: CCSD(T) extrapolated to the basis-set limit (triazine-fitted exponents), on RI-MP2/TZVPP geometries

uncertainty.basis: none stated by the source; about 1 kcal/mol is the disagreement with Fogarasi 2008 on tautomer 3a. Reported, never folded into a tolerance.

systems.notes: The primary multi-state, close-energy row. Structures were read from the paper's Fig. 1 (2a/2b hydroxy-amino, 3a/3b imino-oxo with both ring N-H).

systems.name: Acetylacetone, enol versus diketo, gas phase

source.locator: Supporting Information, electronic energies of the labelled MP2/cc-pVTZ calculations (enol and diketo)

reference.method: MP2/cc-pVTZ, geometry optimized at the same level
reference.zero: the enol (the lowest in the source)

uncertainty.basis: spread between this MP2/cc-pVTZ value (4.849) and the same paper's B3LYP/aug-cc-pVTZ value (6.481), read from the same SI. Evidence of method dependence, not a formal interval.

variants.label: enol
variants.locator: SI, E(MP2) of the MP2/cc-pVTZ enol calculation

variants.label: diketo
variants.locator: SI, E(MP2) of the MP2/cc-pVTZ diketo calculation

systems.notes: The SI's own labelled energies are the primary data, not the main-text Table 1: Table 1 prints B3LYP 6.48 under 6-31G(d,p) and 6.24 under aug-cc-pVTZ, while the SI's energies give 6.26 and 6.48, so the paper contradicts itself on those two labels. MP2/cc-pVTZ (4.849) agrees in both places and is the single declared level. The reference enol is the intramolecularly hydrogen-bonded form; the application starts from one embedded geometry and may not reach it.

systems.name: Acetaldimine versus vinylamine, gas phase

source.locator: Table 1, CCSD(T)//MP2/aug-pVTZ, /pV5Z row, system 4 (the paper's own best value is 3.0-3.1)

uncertainty.basis: the source's own statement that the aug-cc-pVQZ and cc-pV5Z values differ by 0.06 kcal/mol (3.03 versus 3.08 from the printed energies).

systems.notes: Absolute energies are reconstructed from the table's 'E + 132' header as -(132 + printed value); only their difference is used. The source does not state the imine N-H configuration in the table.

systems.name: 2-Pyridone versus 2-hydroxypyridine, gas phase

source.locator: Table 4, cc-pVQZ row (absolute CCSD(T) energies of 8.1 and 8.2)

reference.method: CCSD(T)/cc-pVQZ as labelled in Table 4, on PBE0-D3(BJ)/def2-TZVP geometries; the paper states that its 'CCSD(T)' is DLPNO-CCSD(T) and the table does not say which form Table 4 used

uncertainty.basis: spread between the paper's two CBS extrapolations (2.48 from cc-pVDZ/TZ, 1.96 from cc-pVTZ/QZ); the cc-pVQZ value itself is 0.11 from the 3/4 extrapolation.

systems.notes: Promoted from optional to required because a modern gas-phase electronic-energy source now exists (Goller 2022; the paper states its energy differences are electronic, with the free-energy contribution computed separately in Table 6). The pair is famously hard for hybrid DFT; see tolerance_evidence.

systems.name: Formamide versus formamidic acid, gas phase (lopsided sanity row)

uncertainty.basis: the source states its CCSD(T) values are stable within 0.2 kcal/mol across the largest bases.

systems.notes: Reported and never gating: a gap this large is ranked correctly by almost any method, so passing it proves little.

systems.name: Acetaldehyde versus vinyl alcohol, gas phase (sanity row)

uncertainty.basis: the source's own statement that CCSD(T) and CCSD differ by 0.2 kcal/mol for this system.

corroboration_only.doi_status: not printed in the supplied file; not recorded
corroboration_only.why_not_a_row: 1990 CISD/DZP; its own cited literature spans +2.06 to -3.46 kcal/mol, about 5 kcal/mol. Too uncertain to gate anything.

corroboration_only.doi_status: supplied by a review and not printed in the file; the title and authors were checked against the file
corroboration_only.why_not_a_row: CCSD(T) in two small bases on SCF geometries (3.2 kJ/mol = 0.76 kcal/mol in the larger); its 'best estimate' of 4.7 kJ/mol adds a SCF zero-point correction, so it is not an electronic energy.
Its tautomerization dE is a zero-point-inclusive total energy (CCSD/6-311++G** and aug-cc-pVDZ, 5-9 kJ/mol favouring 2-hydroxypyridine), so it is not the declared electronic quantity.
A cytosine dynamics study that cites CCSD(T) ranges relative to 2b; a secondary citation, used only to size the disagreement on tautomer 3a.
HF/BLYP; its quoted 0.008725 a.u. includes zero-point corrections.
B3LYP-D3/aug-cc-pVQZ over six tautomers with the second lowest more than 10 kcal/mol up: a lopsided DFT cross-check, not a reference.
Solution and vacuum FREE-energy ratios from a machine-learned potential: a different physical quantity from a gas-phase electronic energy.
